title: AI search visibility check
description: Which AI crawlers a site's robots.txt lets in, whether it has an llms.txt, whether buyer searches reach it, and what to fix first. Every verdict quotes what was read.

brand.description: the name searched for, from the input or the home page

status.description: not_found: the host answered 404 (no robots.txt, so every crawler is allowed); unreachable: the fetch failed

verdict.description: blocked: Disallow: / applies to it; partly_blocked: some paths are disallowed; unknown: robots.txt could not be read

rule.description: the robots.txt lines that decide it, quoted (its User-agent group, or the * group it falls to); null when there is no robots.txt or it could not be read

note.description: what the file holds (its first heading, how many links), or the status the fetch gave

result.description: site_listed: a result is on the site; named_by_others: only another site's result names the brand; not_found: neither; search_failed: the search answered an error

position.description: the site's first result's place in the list, 1 first; null when not listed

url.description: that result's URL, or the other site's result that names the brand; null otherwise

top_domains.description: the domains of the first results, in order

fix.description: what to change, concretely: the robots.txt lines to add or remove, the file to publish, the page to write

evidence.description: what was read that shows it: a quoted robots.txt line, a fetch status, a search's result list

report_markdown.description: the audit for a person: the fix list first, then the crawler table, llms.txt, the searches, and what was not checked
